question: Does deterministic structured verification reduce unsupported assertions at matched question coverage on invented engineering documents?
population: Fifteen fixed synthetic error templates, disjoint document/entity/source families; no empirical model or engineering-population claim.
independent_unit: source family; claims and template cases within it are correlated
answerer: scripted fixed-answer-v1, same answers/confidence across all controlled arms
retrieval_budget: same supplied exhaustive local corpus; at most 100 authorized relevant sources, no external retrieval
primary_outcomes: unsupported assertions among asserted factual claims
correct questions per scheduled question at matched coverage
matching: same answered count as strict abstention within split; deterministic ranking descending support fraction or raw confidence, row_id tie break; report selection IDs
power_policy: Pilot paired variance estimates sample needs; fixed 24 test and 12 shifted families are a bounded descriptive allocation, not powered superiority proof.
multiple_hypotheses: Joint descriptive outcomes; no confirmatory significance declaration for H1/H2/H3 or multiplicity-adjusted superiority claim.
calibration: five fixed bins, Laplace smoothing, correctness event all required factual claims correct; calibration split only; no shifted-domain probability promotion
stopping: run every scheduled local arm once; no early stopping, retries or additional samples; exceptions fail release and preserve partial output
exclusions: No empirical answerers, third-party benchmark datasets or human labels. Missing inputs are explicit failures, never successful-case filtering.
audit: Independent pilot and stratified final human annotations pending; executable known answers are provisional, not a substitute.
product_gate: Not eligible pending independent human annotations and a separately approved operational risk/coverage/cost policy. No physical-control authority.
